title: What does a stale part of an aggregate index do?
body:
Today, when is_current says the index beside an input is stale, sail's index_of in input.rs builds a fresh Index in memory and writes nothing to disk. It prints nothing and raises no error.

For an aggregate:

1. Rebuild the stale part in memory, as today for one file. Cost: one edit to one of a thousand files triggers a scan the caller never asked for and never sees.
2. Refuse and name the part. Cost: the caller runs sail index again before the command works.

Lean: refuse and name the part. libsail reports stale parts as positions and sail decides what to do. The one-file behaviour deserves the same question in its own issue.
